parameter_source_contract.rule: Every runtime parameter must declare current source tier and upgrade rule before being treated as production-ready.

london.binding_basis: Batch9 v1 sample evidence and runtime skeleton freeze London as the default session binding for the first implementation pass.
london.calendar_basis: Use a London session calendar aligned to Europe/London local date.
london.dst_handling: Timezone-aware conversion is mandatory; DST shifts must be resolved from Europe/London rather than hard-coded UTC offsets.

new_york.binding_basis: Batch9 v1 sample evidence already uses New York as the second supported reference session for runtime demonstration.
new_york.calendar_basis: Use a New York session calendar aligned to America/New_York local date.
new_york.dst_handling: Timezone-aware conversion is mandatory; DST shifts must be resolved from America/New_York rather than hard-coded UTC offsets.

session_id.source_basis: Batch9 v1 freezes london as the default runtime session binding for the first implementation pass, while still allowing later expansion through the binding registry.
session_id.upgrade_rule: Keep london as the v1 default binding; add new session ids through the registry and open a new version if semantics or calendars change.

session_timezone.source_basis: The london -> Europe/London mapping is frozen in the v1 session binding registry and matches the current sample evidence.
session_timezone.upgrade_rule: Keep timezone derived from the v1 registry; if DST policy or exchange calendar handling changes, record it in notes and open a new version.

opening_range_window_minutes.source_basis: Current v1 contract freezes a 30-minute OR window for the first runtime skeleton and sample evidence.
opening_range_window_minutes.upgrade_rule: If another session template is adopted, record the new window in notes and open a new version if semantics change.
